theorem_title: A fixed coprime denominator cannot recur forever
natural_language_statement:
Let $a,b\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $\gcd(b,a)=1$ and $b>1$, and let $y:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ satisfy $y_0>0$. Then

$$
\neg\bigl(\forall i\in\mathbb N,\ b y_{i+1}=a y_i\bigr).
$$

This excludes an infinite sequence obeying this single recurrence, rather than arbitrary sequences of different affine blocks.
